project.name: Mediterranean Garden House — Live v3 · Stage 5 continuation

slice.name: Asymmetric Mediterranean Garden House
slice.concept: A single-storey Mediterranean garden house formed as a connected asymmetric L around a sheltered, inward-looking garden. The longer social wing combines open-plan kitchen, dining and living spaces with generous garden glazing and a covered veranda; the shorter private wing provides three bedrooms and two bathrooms along calm, comfortable circulation. Warm ivory plaster, pale limestone detailing and terracotta pitched roofs establish a clear main-roof hierarchy without detached structures or changes in terrain.
hierarchy: A dominant pitched-roof social wing anchors the composition and contains the open-plan kitchen, dining and living rooms facing the sheltered garden.
A lower, perpendicular private wing forms the second arm of the L, containing three bedrooms, two bathrooms and a quiet internal circulation spine.
A recessed shaded entrance sits at the inside bend of the L, mediating between arrival and the protected garden court.
A covered veranda extends from the social wing toward the garden, with the terrace and modest pool positioned as integrated outdoor rooms rather than separate objects.
slice.roofLanguage: Terracotta clay-tile pitched roofs give the house its Mediterranean character. A broad, dominant main roof covers the social wing, while a lower perpendicular pitched roof distinguishes the bedroom wing. Deep eaves shade glazing and veranda edges; roof junctions remain simple and legible, reinforcing the asymmetric L-shaped massing.
slice.entrance: A shaded, recessed entrance is placed at the protected inner corner of the L. Pale limestone threshold, surround and restrained wall detailing give arrival a durable civic emphasis, while the approach remains deliberately modest and sheltered beneath the roof overhang.
slice.outdoorLiving: The covered veranda faces directly into the sheltered garden and connects seamlessly to the open-plan kitchen, dining and living area through room-proportioned glazing. A limestone-toned terrace expands beside the veranda for dining and lounging, while a modest swimming pool is set within the garden court with clear sightlines from the social rooms.
slice.landscape: The flat site is treated as a restrained Mediterranean garden: clipped low hedging, gravel-edged planting beds, small groups of drought-tolerant shrubs, aromatic herbs and a limited number of slender shade trees. Planting frames the sheltered court, softens pool edges and preserves open arrival space around the connected house volumes.

intentions: The shaded entrance foyer forms a calm threshold at the protected inner corner of the L-shaped plan.
The kitchen, dining and living rooms form a continuous garden-facing social sequence opening toward the covered veranda.
The flexible garden lounge extends the social wing and can support quiet reading, informal gathering or poolside entertaining.
A dedicated private hall keeps all bedroom doors separate from the open social rooms.
The main bedroom has a private ensuite, while the shared bathroom is directly accessible from the bedroom hall for bedrooms two and three.
Bedroom glazing faces the sheltered east garden side, with the social rooms maintaining long views across the veranda and pool garden.

slice.statement: A coherent single-storey Mediterranean garden house in warm ivory stucco, arranged as an asymmetric L around its sheltered outdoor court. The long social wing is crowned by the dominant terracotta gable roof and opens generously to the shaded veranda, terrace and pool garden. A lower perpendicular bedroom wing is calmer and more private, while the recessed limestone-framed foyer marks the protected inner corner arrival.
intentions: The social wing remains the unmistakable roof crown.
Lower private roofs make a quiet perpendicular wing.
Deep eaves shade the principal garden glazing.
Pale limestone defines the entrance portal, plinth and window surrounds.
Restrained shutters temper the more private elevations.
The veranda is a shaded extension of open-plan living.

slice.statement: A restrained Mediterranean outdoor composition extends the covered veranda into a pale limestone terrace for dining and lounging, with a modest turquoise pool held in the retained garden reservation and read clearly from the social rooms. Broad shade trees, clipped hedge frontage, gravel-edged aromatic planting and open lawn panels preserve the sheltered court’s calm character while keeping the entrance court open and legible.
intentions: Retain the pool as an integrated garden-court room within the social-wing reservation, with pale limestone surround and clear social-room sightlines.
Use restrained gravel-edged beds of drought-tolerant shrubs and aromatic herbs to frame the court and soften pool edges without closing views.
Keep the straight arrival drive and limestone entrance court open; a clipped hedge provides the required frontage definition.
Group six medium canopy trees for measured shade and a Mediterranean garden character, keeping the veranda and lawn panels sunlit.
Extend the veranda’s social life onto the limestone terrace with a four-seat dining setting, compact lounge group and two poolside sunbeds.
